fields.description:
Portable Python public-API surface drift gate (griffe-check-style, test-linked).

## Context / Problem

rebar's Python public API is described by two hand-authored docs (`docs/api-stability.md`,
`docs/reuse-surface.md`). `docs/reuse-surface.md` needs recurring manual upkeep (touched by
most RP-04 slices). The only automated guard is `tests/unit/test_reuse_surface_doc.py`
(ticket f5df): it hardcodes a curated SUBSET of signatures (signing, prompt library,
runner/contracts, workflow executor) and must be hand-edited in lockstep with every
signature change — narrow, and a manual burden. The config-key half of the original audit
is already delivered (sibling ticket 3199 shipped `scripts/gen_config_reference.py` +
`docs/config-reference.md` with a portable test-based drift gate) and is OUT of scope here.

## Approach

Add a `griffe check`-style **public-API surface drift gate** — snapshot the current public
surface into a committed baseline and fail on any diff — implemented with the same
self-contained, pure-stdlib introspection the repo already uses (`inspect`/`importlib`, as
in `tests/unit/test_reuse_surface_doc.py` and `scripts/gen_config_reference.py`). This is the
direct analog of the existing config-key drift gate and avoids adding `griffe` (or any new)
dependency; a self-contained approach is already proven portable and idiomatic here. We do
NOT build a generated Markdown API reference — the OSS evidence (griffe/mkdocstrings
ecosystem, setuptools-scm's `api-check`) shows the high-ROI move is a surface diff gate, not
an auto-generated doc. The hand-authored `docs/api-stability.md` / `docs/reuse-surface.md`
stay the curated narrative; the gate guards the surface, the prose stays human.

- New `scripts/gen_api_surface.py`: introspects the surface, `--update` writes the committed
  baseline JSON, `--check` (default) diffs live vs baseline and exits non-zero on drift with a
  clear "run `--update`" remediation message. Mirrors `scripts/gen_config_reference.py`'s
  `main([...])`/`--check` shape.
- New `tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json`: the committed baseline snapshot.
- New `tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py`: the portable unit-tier test that fails under
  `make test` (no CI-provider dependency) when the surface drifts. It runs the authoritative
  check in a clean subprocess so it reflects the real installed surface (immune to the unit
  tier's autouse `rebar.append_session_log` monkeypatch in `tests/unit/conftest.py:86`).
- Delete `tests/unit/test_reuse_surface_doc.py`; the new baseline captures its whole subset
  automatically and dedicated subsumption assertions prove no coverage is lost.

**Source-of-truth rule (pinned):** the guarded surface is the union, over a pinned `MODULES`
list, of each module's public members — `module.__all__` when defined (the `rebar` facade and
`rebar.signing`/`rebar.llm.workflow.executor` define one), else every non-underscore attribute
the module OWNS (`__module__` is that module/submodule, or a module-level constant with no
`__module__`), excluding imported re-exports and submodules. `MODULES` = the `rebar` facade
(`src/rebar/__init__.py:171` `__all__`) plus the reuse subsystems documented in
`docs/reuse-surface.md`: `rebar.signing`, `rebar.llm.runner`, `rebar.llm.contracts`,
`rebar.llm.findings`, `rebar.llm.prompting.prompts`, `rebar.llm.workflow.executor`. Per symbol
the baseline pins: callable parameter list (name + kind + default-repr), class bases +
dataclass fields + public-method signatures, and the value of pinned immutable constants
(guards e.g. `prompts.FRONT_MATTER_KEYS`, `prompts.EXECUTION_MODES`). The baseline is stored as
committed JSON at `tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json` and updated only via
`python scripts/gen_api_surface.py --update`.

## Scope

- `scripts/gen_api_surface.py` (new) — the introspection + `--check`/`--update` gate.
- `tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json` (new) — the committed surface baseline.
- `tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py` (new) — the portable drift + subsumption test.
- `tests/unit/test_reuse_surface_doc.py` (deleted) — subsumed by the new gate.
- `docs/reuse-surface.md` — update the one-line note that points readers at the old test so it
  names the new gate + baseline + update command.

## Testing

Portable unit-tier tests (`make test`, no CI-provider dependency):
- Committed baseline is current: the gate `--check` exits 0 in a clean subprocess.
- RED→GREEN drift detection: injecting a removed symbol, an added symbol, and a renamed
  parameter each makes `--check`/`diff_surface` report the drift (exit 1); an identical
  surface reports no drift.
- Baseline-update path: `--update` writes the surface then `--check` is clean; a deliberately
  stale baseline trips `--check` and re-running `--update` accepts the intended change.
- Subsumption: the exact signing / prompt-library / runner-contract / workflow-executor subset
  the deleted `test_reuse_surface_doc.py` hardcoded is still asserted present in the surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A portable test in `tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py` runs under `make test` with no
      CI-provider dependency and asserts the live public Python API surface matches the
      committed baseline `tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json`, failing on any removed/renamed
      public symbol or changed signature. Oracle: `make test` collects the test; the gate
      subprocess `python scripts/gen_api_surface.py --check` exits 0 on a clean tree.
- [x] The gate derives the surface from the pinned source-of-truth rule stated in Approach
      (`MODULES` public members via `__all__`-or-owned). Oracle: `test_baseline_file_is_committed_and_wellformed`
      asserts every pinned module appears in the baseline.
- [x] The hardcoded-subset assertions in `test_reuse_surface_doc.py` are removed and subsumed
      with no loss of coverage. Oracle: that file no longer exists; the four `test_subsumes_*`
      tests assert the same signing/prompt/runner/workflow signatures are guarded.
- [x] An intentional surface change is accommodated by the documented `--update` step,
      exercised by a test. Oracle: `test_intentional_change_is_accommodated_by_updating_the_baseline`
      shows a stale baseline fails `--check` and passes after `--update`.
- [x] RED→GREEN: a test proves the gate catches an injected surface drift (added/removed public
      symbol, renamed param). Oracle: `test_check_trips_when_a_public_symbol_is_removed` /
      `_added` / `test_check_trips_when_a_signature_changes` assert exit 1 and the named drift line.
